**Severity:** error · **Area:** Imports / helpers / route modules (`RV3xxx`) · **Quick fix:** yes

## Message

The diagnostic reads:

```text
Untagged server export `{name}`: route server code is a wrapper call — `export const {export} = {wrapper}({argument})` with `import { {wrapper} } from "@rivetjs/router"`
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

Wrap the export in its @rivetjs/router wrapper call: serverLoad → export const loader = `load(…)`, serverGuard → access = `guard(…)`, serverActions → forms = `actions({ … })`, serverEntries → paths = `entries(…)`, serverHeaders → responseHeaders = `headers(…)`, onRequest → middleware = `onRequest(…)`, onGet → GET = `onGet(…)` (same for onPost … onOptions). The export name is free; `rivet migrate server-exports` rewrites a whole app.

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
export const serverLoad = () => ({ n: 1 });
export default () => <p />;
```

```tsx prefer
import { load } from "@rivetjs/router";
export const loader = load(() => ({ n: 1 }));
export default () => <p />;
```

## Quick fix

The [language service](../guides/tooling/language-service.md) (editor) and the MCP `check_code` tool offer this code action:

- rivetWrapServerExport: Wrap in `load(…)` (renames the export and its in-file references, adds the import).

## When it is reported

serverExports option (route modules) and the language service (files under the manifest routesDir). Sibling \*.server.ts names (load, GET …) without wrappers fail at the first request instead (server/module.ts).
